study_identification_part.si_4_title: Rightward brain structural asymmetry in young children with autism

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used data from the Shanghai Autism Early Developmental (SAED) Cohort, collected at two sites: Site 1 with a Philips Ingenia MRI scanner (283 children) and Site 2 with a Siemens Verio MRI scanner (747 children). Total sample: 1030 children including 563 ASD with DD/ID, 212 ASD without DD/ID, 36 DD/ID only, and 219 typically developing (TD) children.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Participants were recruited from a neurodevelopmental project - Shanghai Autism Early Development Cohort [40]." ... "The MRI data of 283 children (164 ASD with DD/ID, 74 ASD without DD/ID, and 45 TD) were collected at site 1 with a Philips Ingenia MRI scanner. And MRI data of 747 children (399 ASD with DD/ID, 138 ASD without DD/ID, 36 DD/ID, and 174 TD) were collected at site 2 with a Siemens Verio MRI scanner."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: TD children (247 mentioned for model training) were used to train the normative models using Gaussian Process Regression with 5-fold cross-validation. The three patient groups (ASD with DD/ID, ASD without DD/ID, DD/ID only) were then evaluated against these normative models to extract individual deviation Z-scores for clinical analysis.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "GPR models of GMV asymmetry for each ROI were trained based on 247 TDs with age and sex as covariates. Fivefold cross-validation was conducted to avoid overfitting and obtain optimal parameters. In this way, we generated developmental normative GMV asymmetry distributions in TD individuals. Then, we put the individual GMV asymmetry metric and covariate variables (age and sex) of children in the ASD with DD/ID, ASD without DD/ID and DD/ID only groups into the generated models and obtained the individual Z scores"

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The paper reports 219 TD children in the sample characteristics (Supplementary Table S2), but mentions 247 TDs in the methods section for normative model training. This discrepancy (219 vs 247) may be due to different quality control stages or reporting inconsistencies. The methods explicitly state '247 TDs' were used for training the normative model with 5-fold cross-validation.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are reported for the 219 TD children in the sample. The paper provides mean +/- SD and age range. Train-phase specific statistics are not reported separately due to 5-fold cross-validation approach where different subsets were used in each fold. The age range for train-phase is inferred to be the same as overall since children were randomly split.
